svg.title: Joint generation and an internal flip with an extra relative commutant
svg.desc: Exact quotient-group construction in Section 5A. The quotient kills one free generator. Kernel conjugacy computes the generated algebra. An internal basis permutation swaps the commuting finite copies. An explicit graph vector shows the second copy misses a relative-commutant unitary. Stabilizing gives copies of the entire properly infinite factor with joint generation and an internal flip; relative-commutant equality still fails.

g.text: Generation and a flip do not force relative commutation
Exact operators and graph subspace · Section 5A · a different free-group member
Γ = F(a₀,a₁,...) and Δ = F(b₀,b₁,...)
Quotient π: a₀ ↦ e, aₙ₊₁ ↦ bₙ · H = ker π
Separate isomorphism β: aₙ ↦ bₙ · β does not kill a₀.
Lemma 5A.2: every nonidentity H-conjugacy orbit is infinite.
Two commuting normal finite copies on ℓ²(Γ) ⊗ ℓ²(Δ)
A generated by λg ⊗ 1; B generated by ρg ⊗ ρπ(g).
A ∨ B = E = B(ℓ²(Γ)) ⊗̄ RΔ · type II∞
Kernel coefficients force E′ = 1 ⊗ λ(Δ)′′. No larger commutant is omitted.
Full computation: Lemmas 5A.1–5A.3 and Theorem 5A.4.
Internal permutation J: (x,q) ↦ (x⁻¹,qπ(x)⁻¹)
J² = 1 · J ∈ E · J(λg ⊗ 1)J = ρg ⊗ ρπ(g)
J commutes with 1 ⊗ λv; it is the exact symmetry in Lemma 5A.5.
The graph detects the missing relative-commutant operator.
Gπ = closed span of δx ⊗ δπ(x) · every B-generator preserves Gπ.
(e,e) ∈ graph of π
Z = 1 ⊗ ρb₀
(e,b₀⁻¹) is outside the graph.
Z ∈ A′ ∩ E, but Z ∉ B · Proposition 5A.6
Stabilize with two infinite matrix coordinates L = ℓ²(ℕ).
P ≅ M̃ ≅ Q · S = FL ⊗ J ∈ M̃ · S² = 1 · SPS = Q
P ∨ Q = M̃ · Q ⊊ P′ ∩ M̃ · P ⊊ Q′ ∩ M̃
Theorem 5A.7 transports the normal endomorphism and symmetry to M₀ = B(K) ⊗̄ RΓ.
Source verdict: this generating pair fails the relative-commutant clause.
It does not rule out every possible pair in Connes's Corollary 11 (author PDF 44–45).
